The proposed default recall includes only accepted, unexpired, applicable entries in permitted scopes. Active, unexpired handovers belong in an explicit handover view labeled as unreviewed work. These are target behaviors, not verified capabilities.

No. The proposal distinguishes human acceptance from evidence verification: verified_at remains null unless the evidence was actually checked. Model-assigned confidence is not verification.

The proposal calls for separate deployments or separate credentials and stores from the beginning. Publishing private entries to a team must be explicit and reviewed, with a new destination identity and provenance link.

Proposed phase 1A is limited to one repository, one owner, one writer host, and 20–30 owner-reviewed, non-sensitive records with sources and stable IDs. Clients must be verified as read/search-only or the unrestricted server stays disabled. Agent capture, automatic lifecycle filtering, review enforcement, concurrent writes, complete revision-history portability, and multi-user authorization are deferred. Text queries permit a documented local-embedding exception, with no hosted provider.

The proposed contract scopes idempotency keys to the authenticated caller and operation. Identical retries must return the original result; reuse with a different payload must fail. Retrying an accepted proposal returns its original resulting revision.

No under the proposed contract. Submitted candidate content and metadata are immutable; corrections require a new proposal. Acceptance or rejection can still be recorded.

The proposal recommends evaluating Basic Memory in a read-only, personal recall experiment with a curated corpus before building a custom engine. Recall success does not establish capture or team compliance.

Under the proposed workflow, the first acceptance advances the record beyond revision four. The second acceptance must conflict and leave its proposal pending because its stored base_revision is stale. A new proposal against the current revision is required.
